speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Hi, everyone. If you have one, raise your hand and  we'll come to you. If you're ready, go to Sam. Hi,  
Sam. Fortunately for the game, is that a bit  of a relief now, just to get that second place  
Champions League sorted? Yes, that's what we  wanted to achieve today. We had a few objectives,  
finishing second, finishing the Champions League  spots, and as well finishing the season in front  
of our people in the right manner with the right  results. And those two things have been achieved.  
What, obviously, for the players and you, you  need to break this, but for the rest of the club,  
what needs to be done now? Well, first of all, we  have one more game to play and to finish it in the  
right way and winning in Southampton is going  to be really important again. And then, yeah,  
go on holidays, time to reset first, bring the  temperature down a little bit. It's been a long,  
long season. And I start to think and reflect  in everything that we have planned is the  
right one. I start to make some steps, some  action and come back here fresh on day one,  
ready to go again. On the pitch to the supporters  after the game, you seemed very emotional. It was  
a very powerful message that you gave. Can  you talk about your sort of, I don't know,  
emotions and what you've gone through this season  and maybe some sense of disappointment but also  
optimism? It was emotional because the way I feel  and it's great. We had a dream, I said it out  
there. It was to deliver a big trophy this season  for our people and because I think that the team  
deserves it as well in the journey that we've been  together in the last three, four years. We haven't  
achieved that and there's a lot of factors and a  lot of situation that we've been through for the  
last 9½ months for that not happening. But make  sure that we still value a lot of the incredible  
things this club is doing, the team is doing,  the players are doing, the way we are competing  
and the consistency that we are showing. Because  if we are not able to see that, that's a really,  
really dangerous thing to do. Just expecting  just something and playing. If we don't,  
that's a really dangerous thing. And I know they  don't want us there where we are now, knocking on  
the door every year and make sure that we can  see clarity. We stay very disciplined and very  
clear and ambitious with what we want to do in the  summer. So what would be your overall thought and  
reflection on the season when you consider that?  When you talk about we must get how you did out  
there, we mustn't be blurred in our vision. I  would leave that for the summer. I've done it  
in the dressing room and for me it's very clear,  but I'm there every day. I know what we've been  
through for 9½ months. I know what we've done. I  know very well the history of this Premier League  
and the teams that they've been not in 30% of the  situation that we've been in, they have collapsed,  
completely collapsed. And we haven't. And I really  value that because that shows that we have built  
something that is very, very sustainable and  consistent. Regardless, some people doesn't  
like to see it. Simon, Standard. Mikel, we  heard from Josh a comment before we came in  
the programme talking about the plan to invest  this summer and then win those major trophies.  
Do you feel going into that window you've got  the backing from the owners that you need? Yeah,  
but that's not something new. I think they always  back the team, the club in the best possible way  
and it's not going to be different in the summer.  We have to be very smart with the decisions that  
we take. Obviously, we need players because the  squad is really short and on top of that we are  
losing four or five players that they're going  to end contracts and the loans are finished. So  
we need to be sharp, again, very disciplined  in what we want to do and make sure that we  
are a stronger next season. But the fact that  you've now officially got that Champions League  
qualification mean, you can literally tomorrow  start executing that plan because financially.  
I mean, the plan is done and the time will be  dictated by many parties, many circumstances that  
unfortunately we don't control. But we have great  people in charge of that. Andrea is going to be  
leading that with the board and ownership. And  as well, make sure that the ones that we have,  
they feel valued, they feel loved, make sure that  they want to continue with us in the right manner.  
And then the whole environment that is excited,  you know, that is not just about now if we next,  
because we cannot start a season like that. And  I want to feel that from day one and I'm going  
to be very insistive of that. Of course, injuries  have been a massive part of your season this time  
around. You said on TV about injuries are on the  teams, and the teams are finished 16th and 17th,  
but not this season, and in previous seasons  in the history, and 8th. And 5th, missing one  
or two players only. Yeah, yeah. So you said  16-17, does that spread the United? No, no, no,  
no. That was in the past. In the past. And in the  past, in five years ago, 10 years ago, look in the  
memory and see what has happened in this league.  Do you think next season, without such injuries,  
obviously? I don't know. I don't know. I will try.  I can promise, I will do my very best. I will live  
my life here. I will give everything. I will  get every drop of everybody there. I squeeze it  
to get the best. But promise, I cannot promise. I  cannot. Any manager is going to promise tomorrow.  
Next season I'm going to be in the Premier League  or the Champions League. If I have to do that, I  
don't do it because I cannot promise anybody that.  My best and the best of this play that they're  
going to try and go mad chasing that, I guarantee  you that that's going to happen. Tom, from London.  
Hi, Mikel. We've had the difficulties that we've  had this season. When you were at Union Chapel  
last night and you walked out on that stage with  the fans that were there, I was lucky enough to be  
in that room and hear that noise. Do you get the  sense that those fans that were there so close do  
get the sense and have that belief that we will go  again, they will go again next season and be able  
to do it? Yeah, it was a really special evening.  I was very lucky to be there as well. And yeah,  
I do feel it. And we don't take it for granted and  we want to sustain that and give them joy and then  
they can feel proud about this football team, the  individuals, the values that we have as a football  
club and how we represent it and then win. And if  we can achieve all of that in once, then great.  
I got James here. Mikel, you talked about creating  the love from day one. Have you sort of felt the  
need to maybe stress a bit of patience, get that  message about patience and not get frustrated by  
finishing second, but keeping everybody on board  and look at how far you can and look at that. I  
don't know. I don't think it's now we finish  second for the third season. In the last three  
seasons, there is one team that has been better  than us in total points, which is Manchester City,  
with the best team in the history of this league  by a mile. And we are there. And Liverpool has  
a trophy. We don't have a trophy. We are in the  Champions League semi-final for the last 16 years.  
And we are unsatisfied and upset. And it's not  good enough. Great. Let's go for the next thing,  
but I think we're in the right trajectory,  hopefully. Okay, last couple. Phil from PA. And  
just sort of following off on that, do you feel  that the fans are still 100% behind you and this  
group of players? That's what I feel, but I don't  know. The ones that I see every day in the street,  
the ones that they contact me, the ones that I see  there, I would say that 100%, but they want more  
because we have set expectations. And they've seen  the team that is capable against any opposition to  
compete against them. So we need to believe  that we're going to do it together. Finally,  
Nick from Hayters. I've got talking of injuries  made three significant substitutions with coming  
on Kieran Tierney and Jorginho. Just a  word on those players and your... Well,  
the first one because of an injury of Willie. I  think he felt something in his hamstring in the  
first half, unfortunately, so we had to make the  substitution. And with the other two, yeah, Kai,  
I mean, he's been incredibly fast in his recovery.  I think the doctors were a bit, is it too early,  
but he's been pushing it and he thought he could  help the team. And with Kieran as well, you know,  
he had a very special circumstances the way he  had to come back and settle in the team again  
after four months out. And he's been really  good with the group and he has contributed  
in every possible way to help us and very grateful  for that. And quite emotional for them as well  
because possibly their last games. Yeah, we had a  few in that dressing room that probably is going  
to be the last time that they put that shirt at  the Emirates. So I've been there and make sure  
that we are close to them and I'm very grateful  to them as well. Okay, thank you. Yeah, thank you.
title: Mikel Arteta post-match press conference | Arsenal 1-0 Newcastle United
